method: Each exercise rendered in the athlete look at six phases of its loop (start, early, middle, deepest/peak, return, end) and reviewed by eye against its written instructions, with doubtful ones re-rendered at 300-800 px and their joint and equipment positions read from the motion engine (hand-to-equipment distance, floor contact, travel, joint angles). Automated motion checks: tests/unit/exercise-motion*.test.ts and exercise-form.test.ts. Reviewed by Claude (AI), spot-checked; not reviewed by a coach and not approved by the owner.

90-90-hip-switch.note: Front view: the front leg is foreshortened and hard to read, hands hover beside the hips, and mid-switch the legs disappear behind the pelvis.

agility-ladder-drills.note: No ladder is drawn (props are empty), so it reads as an ordinary slow jog rather than quick foot placements through a ladder.

air-bike-sprint.note: Knee stays bent about 80 degrees at the bottom of the stroke, which is the listed 'seat too low' mistake (handles are drawn correctly).

arm-over-arm-sled-pull.note: The rope stays attached to the right hand only, so whenever the left hand reaches forward it grips air about 50 cm above the rope.

atlas-stone-load.note: Loop resets by fading out with the stone on the platform and fading back in at the floor.

axle-clean-and-press.note: Axle drawn with the older classic plate (heavier gold rim) than the athlete barbell.

band-assisted-pull-up.note: Band drawn as a red line from the bar to the shin over the body; grip direction cannot be drawn.

band-neck-training.note: Shows the extension setup (facing the anchor, band behind the head) only; the band is the older red line.

band-pass-through.note: Side view: the band is seen end-on as a small gold hook at the hands.

band-pull-apart.note: At full stretch the band lies behind the arms and chest and disappears for a moment, so the moving loop looks like the band vanishes.

bear-crawl.note: Hands hover about 15 cm above the floor and the knees are about 30 cm up, so it reads as a crouch with dangling arms, not a bear crawl on hands and feet.

bike-intervals.note: Knee stays bent about 80 degrees at the bottom of the stroke (the listed "seat too low" mistake) and the hands hang in the air with no handlebar drawn.

box-jump.note: Returns to the floor by a cross-fade rather than showing the step-down (neutral, the instructions say to step down).

broad-jump.note: Loop resets with a fade back to the start line after the landing.

cable-crunch.note: At the bottom the head and hands go inside the cable tower frame (kneeling too close to the stack); the curl itself is right.

cable-woodchop.note: Front view cannot show the hip/torso turn or back-foot pivot; written cues cover it.

chin-up.note: Grip direction cannot be drawn (coach-flagged); the label names it.

conventional-deadlift.note: Coach-flagged: start torso on the flat side of normal.

copenhagen-plank.note: Support drawn as a box rather than a bench; isometric hold.

dips.note: Coach-flagged: shoulder position at the bottom; dip bars drawn as a simple frame.

figure-four-stretch.note: The crossed ankle never rests on the opposite thigh: both shins point forward side by side, so it reads as a double knees-to-chest stretch, not a figure-four.

front-squat.note: Side view: the near plate hides the face and rack position (coach-flagged limitation; instructions describe the rack).

hack-squat.note: Machine drawn as a thin rail with the shoulder pad as a gold outline; readable at full size, faint at thumbnail size.

hip-abduction.note: Band is the older red line; hands hover out to the sides instead of resting on the seat.

hip-escape.note: Side view can't show turning onto the side; the figure lies on its back doing a small crunch with a slight hip slide, so the shrimp is not recognisable.

jump-rope.note: Rope is a thin single strand; small hop.

landmine-rotation.note: Hip-side end positions are right, but through the middle both hands leave the bar and spread out wide at chest height.

lateral-bound.note: Lands with both feet on the floor (trailing foot only about 2 cm up) and flies with arms out in a T, so the single-leg skater landing that defines the drill is not shown.

lateral-shuffle.note: The feet only lift and replace in place (pelvis moves about 2 cm, no travel), so it shows stepping on the spot rather than shuffling sideways.

leg-curl.note: Fixed 2026-11-04: the lever and ankle pad are now drawn in front of the legs (machineLever prop), so the resisted curl reads clearly.

leg-extension.note: The roller pad is now drawn in front of the ankle (machineLever), but the lever overlaps the shin and the seat's back pad is hidden, so the machine still reads like a stool; needs a clearer machine drawing.

medicine-ball-rotational-throw.note: At the start the ball floats at the hip away from both hands, and the throw looks like an arm swing on the wall side rather than a hip-led rotation from the far hip.

medicine-ball-scoop-toss.note: Drawn side-on as a squat-and-heave straight up overhead with no wall and no hip rotation, not a rotational scoop into a wall at chest height.

medicine-ball-shot-put.note: The ball floats on the chest about 50 cm from either hand and the throwing arm swings up past the head instead of pushing the ball from the rear shoulder.

neck-isometrics.note: Only the front and back holds can be seen from the side; the side holds are in the text.

pallof-press.note: Front view foreshortens the press toward the camera, so the pressed position looks almost the same as the start (hands just meet at the chest).

pike-push-up.note: At the bottom the forearms lie almost flat on the floor and the head sits over the hands, not in front of them, so it reads like a forearm (dolphin) push-up.

pogo-jumps.note: Hops are only a few centimetres, so at thumbnail size the figure looks almost still.

posing-practice.note: Front relaxed and double-biceps are right, but the third pose has the hands floating out to the sides instead of fists on the waist for a lat spread.

power-clean.note: Side view: plates cover the face and the catch/rack position; bar turnover is very quick but plausible.

pro-agility-shuttle.note: Steps in place between two cones with zero travel and reaches only to knee height, so the 5-10-5 sprints, plants and line touches are not shown.

pull-up.note: Grip direction cannot be drawn (coach-flagged); the label names it.

push-press.note: Side view: the near plate covers the face and front rack position (same limitation as the front squat).

reactive-mirror-drill.note: The feet only lift and replace in place (pelvis moves about 2 cm), so no lateral shuffling or reacting is shown.

rear-delt-fly.note: In side view the dumbbells travel up and forward to the chest with bent elbows, so it reads as a row or front raise; the arms opening out to the sides is not visible.

run-walk-intervals.note: Only the running part is drawn; the walk recovery is in the text.

sandbag-load-over-bar.note: Loop resets by fading out with the bag on the platform and fading back in at the floor.

sandbag-to-shoulder.note: On the way down the bag leaves the hands and falls to the floor while the lifter stands upright, instead of being lowered with control; lap and shoulder positions are right.

seated-leg-curl.note: The roller pad is now drawn behind the ankle in front of the leg (machineLever), but the lever overlaps the calf and the back pad is hidden, so the machine still reads like a stool; needs a clearer machine drawing.

strongman-farmers-walk.note: Handles and plates use the older classic drawing.

sumo-deadlift.note: Coach-flagged: start torso may be lower than many coaches teach.

t-drill.note: Drawn with the same in-place side-step loop as the shuttle: no forward sprint, no lateral shuffle across 10 yards, no backpedal.

thoracic-open-book.note: Drawn from above, but it reads as an all-fours (quadruped) rotation over a raised box (the mat seen from above); the side-lying, knees-stacked setup is not recognisable.

three-cone-drill.note: Same in-place side-step loop as the shuttle: no sprinting, no L-shaped route or turns around the cones.

trap-bar-carry.note: Trap bar plate uses the older classic drawing.

trap-bar-jump.note: The dip is a fairly deep hinge rather than a quarter squat; trap bar plate uses the older classic drawing.

walking-lunge.note: The back foot steps backward and returns while the front foot stays planted, so the loop is a reverse lunge rather than stepping forward into the next lunge; the bottom lunge position is right.

wall-drill.note: The body is piked at the hips with near-vertical legs (about 18 degrees of lean overall) instead of a straight line at about 45 degrees, which is the listed mistake.

worlds-greatest-stretch.note: Between the floor-hand and ceiling-reach positions the arm sweeps forward horizontally like a front reach instead of rotating open.

yoke-carry.note: The yoke is drawn as a single upright with a plate at its foot, seen from the side; readable but stylised.

zercher-carry.note: Side-view plate covers the elbow cradle; the written steps describe it.

zercher-squat.note: Side-view plate covers the elbow cradle; the written steps describe it.
